_doc: AI Story script (horror). This file scaffolds the 7-beat structure. The daily-shorts-pipeline routine fills in 'text', 'keywords', 'title', 'description', 'visual_brief' and 'sound_brief' fields at production time, then runs check_script_structure.py to lint, then make_audio_elevenlabs.py + build_visuals_track.py + build_sound_design.py.

beats.label: hook
beats.purpose_hint: Setup → wrong detail. The wrong detail IS the hook.

sound_brief.ambient_bed: kitchen room tone, refrigerator hum, distant clock tick, silence-dominant
sound_brief.vocal_mood: tight whisper, slow tempo, breath audible on the reveal
sound_brief.mix_note: ambient -22db, sfx hit drops -3db then silence reasserts

beats.text: He smiled. The lamp dimmed when I disagreed back.

visual_brief.subject: kitchen lamp casting a single circle of light on a dining table, husband's silhouette half-visible at the edge
visual_brief.framing: low-angle medium shot, table-level, husband off-center right
visual_brief.lighting: single warm lamp overhead, hard shadow underneath, everything else black
visual_brief.color: near-monochrome, blue-black shadow, single warm highlight on the table

beats.visual_style_hint: static frame, single subject, deep shadow

beats.label: setup
beats.purpose_hint: Ground the listener in normality before the realization

sound_brief.ambient_bed: dining room ambience, plate clinks, faint cutlery, kitchen extractor distant

beats.text: It started small. Two years ago. He asked me to pass the salt. I said in a minute. He didn't speak for the rest of dinner.

visual_brief.subject: dining table with two place settings, salt shaker between them, untouched plates of food
visual_brief.lighting: soft overhead pendant, slightly cool, no shadows
visual_brief.color: muted greens and creams, low saturation

beats.label: build
beats.purpose_hint: Second wrong thing, third wrong thing, escalating

sound_brief.ambient_bed: house at night, low wind through walls, no other sound

beats.text: Last winter the wall clock stopped at three o'clock. He said it was fine. The clock stayed stopped for eleven months.

visual_brief.subject: vintage wall clock with hands frozen at three, mounted on cracked wallpaper
visual_brief.framing: medium close-up, slightly off-axis right, clock centered
visual_brief.lighting: weak window light from frame left, dust visible in beam
visual_brief.color: dust greys, sepia yellows, deep shadow on the wall edges

beats.visual_style_hint: tighter framing, lower light, off-center subject

beats.label: mid_anchor
beats.purpose_hint: Realization — the wrongness is intentional, not coincidence

sound_brief.ambient_bed: complete silence, single distant refrigerator hum, room tone -28db
sound_brief.music_cue: music spike to peak then ABRUPT silence on 'no, actually, I won't'
sound_brief.vocal_mood: tight whisper, almost breathless, slower than baseline on the pivot
sound_brief.mix_note: music sidechain to VO, ABRUPT cut to silence on the word 'won't', let silence breathe

beats.text: Eleven months of nothing breaking, nothing creaking, nothing disagreeing. Then I told him no, actually, I won't.

visual_brief.mood: frozen, sub-zero dread, the moment everything pivots
visual_brief.subject: closed bedroom door at end of dark hallway, a single hand on the doorknob from camera POV
visual_brief.framing: POV first-person, narrow hallway compressing toward the door, low height
visual_brief.lens: 28mm wide, sharp deep focus, slight vignette
visual_brief.lighting: single overhead bulb fifty feet behind camera, door is the brightest object
visual_brief.color: deep blue-black hallway, warm bulb glow only on the door, hand silhouette dark

beats.visual_style_hint: HERO SHOT — first proper look at the threat, partial reveal

beats.label: expand

sound_brief.ambient_bed: fridge hum cuts to dead silence at 0:01, then thin distant air pressure
sound_brief.music_cue: low drone returns at lower intensity, sustained
sound_brief.mix_note: ambient hard cut on fridge stop, music creeps back in, VO dominant

beats.text: The lamp dimmed. The fridge hum cut. Every wall held its breath. And he smiled again, slower this time.

visual_brief.subject: kitchen lamp visibly dimming mid-frame, surrounding shadows growing inward
visual_brief.framing: medium wide, eye-level, lamp centered, edges falling to black
visual_brief.lighting: single lamp source actively dimming through the shot, no fill
visual_brief.color: warm orange dying into blue-black at the edges

beats.visual_style_hint: POV unsteady, breath sound, oppressive shadows

beats.label: payoff

sound_brief.ambient_bed: thin air pressure, distant low rumble, no clock no fridge
sound_brief.music_cue: sustained low drone, no resolution, holds
sound_brief.mix_note: music sustained under VO, ambient very thin, sfx is the only punctuation

beats.text: Whatever lives in this house with us, my husband taught it the rules. I learned them too late.

visual_brief.subject: dim hallway reflection in a darkened mirror, doorknob centered, no figure visible
visual_brief.framing: tight close-up of mirror surface, slight angle, doorknob reflection sharp
visual_brief.lighting: single warm bulb behind the mirror caster, mirror itself dim
visual_brief.color: deep amber on doorknob, surrounding void blue-black

beats.visual_style_hint: single decisive composition, threat now fully visible

beats.label: cta
beats.purpose_hint: FOLLOW-DRIVER (v2): 'Don't [verb] [object]. Follow if you want more.' Warning hook + follow ask in one line

sound_brief.ambient_bed: back to hook ambient: kitchen room tone, fridge hum returns
sound_brief.music_cue: drone resolves to single low tone, fades to ambient
sound_brief.mix_note: match-cut ambient to hook, music tucks under, VO clean

beats.text: Don't disagree with the house. Follow if you want the rules.

visual_brief.mood: loop-back to hook, same composition different light
visual_brief.subject: kitchen lamp casting circle on table, mirror match to hook beat composition
visual_brief.framing: low-angle medium shot identical to hook, husband absent now
visual_brief.lighting: single warm lamp, slightly brighter than hook, room is empty

beats.visual_style_hint: match-cut to the hook composition (loop trigger)

character_continuity_hint: [First-person POV by default. The 'protagonist' is the camera. Brief external glimpses (hands, reflections) are allowed but no full-body shots of the narrator. The THREAT may be partially revealed in mid_anchor and fully shown in payoff — keep its visual design consistent within a video.]
description_lead: A wife learns that something in her house punishes any voice that contradicts her husband's.
hook_anti_patterns: fan-fiction of existing IP (Slenderman, SCP, etc) — original creepypasta ONLY
[mundane setup → wrong detail] structure — flip to [wrong detail → setup]
starting with 'The' / 'A' / 'An' / 'In' — soft and slow for sentence 1
hook_template: [Wrong detail in 4-5 words]. [Mundane context after.] (Lead with the wrongness.)
original_only_rule: NO adapting existing creepypasta IP (Slenderman, SCP, Backrooms, Mr. Wisepuff, etc). Every horror story must be Claude's original micro-fiction. The premise can borrow tropes (haunted house, doppelganger, deep-sea creature, etc) but the specific entity, setting, and prose must be new.

sound_brief_defaults.ambient_bed: room tone, low hum, silence-dominant, refrigerator pulse -28db (let silence speak)
sound_brief_defaults.mix_note: ambient very low so silence reads as silence, hero-beat music spikes to 0.7 then drops to 0 on reveal, SFX hit on the wrong-detail mention
sound_brief_defaults.vocal_mood: tight whisper, slow tempo, breath audible on the reveal

title: Don't Disagree With the House

visual_brief_defaults.color: near-monochrome, blue-black shadows, single warm highlight, high contrast
visual_brief_defaults.lighting: single warm light source against deep shadow, dark frame negative space

visual_palette: near-monochrome, blue-black shadows, single warm light source, high contrast
spoken_text:
He smiled. The lamp dimmed when I disagreed back.

It started small. Two years ago. He asked me to pass the salt. I said in a minute. He didn't speak for the rest of dinner.

Last winter the wall clock stopped at three o'clock. He said it was fine. The clock stayed stopped for eleven months.

Eleven months of nothing breaking, nothing creaking, nothing disagreeing. Then I told him no, actually, I won't.

The lamp dimmed. The fridge hum cut. Every wall held its breath. And he smiled again, slower this time.

Whatever lives in this house with us, my husband taught it the rules. I learned them too late.

Don't disagree with the house. Follow if you want the rules.
